title: Reading Canadian salary guides with Python

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does a cloud architect earn in Quebec City compared to Montreal? The answers sit locked inside PDF salary guides.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the puzzle behind Salary, a data project from the AlgoÉTS club. It turns recruitment-firm salary guides and federal wage tables into data frames.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do you get numbers out of a PDF?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One script per guide edition. It reads the PDF, tracks the current province and region, then splits each line into a job title and three ranges: entry, mid and senior. The result is saved for analysis.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Those are CSV files from the federal Job Bank, covering 2012 to 2022. A Polars script harmonizes the columns across years and prints the best-paid jobs for each one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. In notebooks you can rank jobs, filter engineering roles, compare one job across provinces and regions, and find the biggest regional gaps. A small FastAPI app also serves the guides as JSON.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So it's useful for salary curiosity and for anyone pulling tables from PDFs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The full write-up has the results from the 2023 guide.
